How it works

Use the catalog to identify an exact coding-agent version or service surface, inspect attributed publisher claims and official sources, and compare records without turning evidence coverage into a ranking.

Browse the catalog Compare claims

1. Start with the exact identity

AEC records describe an exact agent/version or rolling service surface at a specific publisher, channel and delivery boundary. Start by selecting the precise identity you need before you inspect claims or compare records.

Publisher
Named publisher
Product
Named agent
Version / surface
Exact version or rolling service
Channel
Recorded when a source identifies one
Delivery boundary
Local, hybrid or hosted

2. Follow each claim to its source

Each record includes publisher claims collected from publisher-controlled official sources. Every claim stays linked to its named source and attached to the exact identity it supports.

  1. Publisher claimA specific statement from an official publisher source.
  2. Official sourceThe named publisher-controlled source where the claim appears.
  3. Applicability boundaryThe version, configuration, platform, model or deployment conditions that limit the claim.

3. Unknown stays visible

If a fact is missing, unresolved or outside the accepted source, it remains unknown in AEC. Unknown does not mean absent: the catalog does not infer or fill gaps.

4. Compare claims, not agents

Comparison aligns exact records and accepted claim categories side by side. It is not a score, ranking, recommendation or proof of capability.

Accepted claim categoryExact record AExact record B
Claim statementShown with its official sourceNo accepted claim under this exact category
ApplicabilityVersion and conditions remain visibleAbsence is not inferred

5. Snapshots, known updates and version history

A readable snapshot date identifies the stable catalog view. Records with known later releases are marked, but a marker does not silently change the reviewed record. A human reviews official sources before changing an identity, and same-surface predecessor and successor records remain available as version history.

  1. Snapshot publishedA dated catalog view provides a stable point of reference.
  2. Known updates markedA marker shows where an official source exposed a later identity after the snapshot review.
  3. Human review before changeThe record changes only after review, and same-surface history remains preserved.

6. What AEC does not establish

AEC organizes attributed publisher claims and official sources. It does not establish:

  • Observed behaviourNo product was installed or run for these source-only records.
  • QualityDocumentation coverage is not a quality measure.
  • SafetyPublisher claims and visible unknowns are not a safety finding.
  • SuitabilityThe catalog does not decide whether an agent fits your task or environment.

7. Inspect the evidence or suggest a correction

Each record page links every accepted claim to its named official source so you can inspect the evidence yourself. If you find an issue, you can suggest a public-safe correction for human review.
